apiReference.title: API
apiReference.subtitle: Everything this panel does is reachable through the API. Nothing is reserved for the interface.
apiReference.keyFamilies: Two families of keys, two levels of access
apiReference.keyFamiliesBody: A personal key (gd_live_) belongs to someone: its scopes bound their rights and can never exceed them. An application key (gd_app_) belongs to no one: its scopes are its rights. The two live in separate tables, behind separate guards, on separate URL prefixes.
apiReference.routingHint: The API is served by the panel domain, under the /api prefix.
apiReference.sameOrigin: Since the panel and the API share an origin, the interface authenticates with its session cookie: no token travels through JavaScript and there is no CORS preflight. Mutating requests do carry an anti-CSRF token, a protection that becomes necessary as soon as a cookie is enough to authenticate.
apiReference.externalClients: External clients authenticate with a key and depend on no cookie. CORS is only opened for origins declared by an OAuth application.
apiReference.keyAuthHint: The access mode for scripts, bots and integrations.
apiReference.keyStorage: The key is shown only once, at creation: only its fingerprint is kept. Every key carries scopes, a list of allowed IP addresses and an expiry date, one year at most. Every request is written to the audit log with the fingerprint used.
apiReference.applicationWarning: These routes ignore ownership. A compromised application key grants access to every server: always restrict it to a list of IP addresses.
apiReference.realtimeHint: The console and the graphs go through a websocket, not the REST API. Ask for a token at <c>POST /servers/{server}/websocket</c>: the response gives the websocket address, opened directly on the machine's daemon, and the token to present there. The token lasts ten minutes and carries only the scopes of the key that asked for it.
apiReference.ssoHint: The panel delegates sign-in to an external OAuth 2.0 provider. It does not issue identities: it recognises the ones presented to it.
apiReference.ssoDirectionValue: The panel is the client. Your provider is the source of truth.
apiReference.ssoExclusiveValue: Password sign-in is refused for everyone, including on this API.
apiReference.sessionOnly: These routes are not restricted by scope: they are closed to API keys, whatever their scopes. Scopes describe server permissions; none speaks about account security.
apiReference.threeChecksBody: The panel draws a random <c>state</c> and compares it on return, otherwise the redirection could be forged. The <c>code_verifier</c> never leaves the panel's server. And <c>redirect_uri</c> must match exactly on both sides: a port or a trailing slash is enough to break the exchange.
apiReference.firstLogin: On first sign-in, a panel account is created and linked to the provider's stable identifier — never to the email address, which a provider may allow to change. If an address the provider declares <c>email_verified</c> already matches an account, the two are reconciled instead of creating a second one. Without that claim no reconciliation happens: it would hand someone else's account to whoever declares their address.
apiReference.errorsHint: The same shape on every route.
apiReference.error400: Invalid request, body or parameters rejected
apiReference.error404: Resource does not exist or is outside the key's perimeter
apiReference.error409: Conflict, for example an action already in progress
apiReference.error429: Rate limit reached, see the Retry-After header
apiReference.webhookSignatureHint: Every callback is signed. A receiver that skips verification accepts anything claiming to come from the panel.
apiReference.webhookToleranceValue: 300 s. Reject beyond that: a captured delivery must not stay replayable.
apiReference.webhookRetriesValue: 7 attempts: 30 s, 2 min, 10 min, 1 h, 6 h, 24 h, then give up.
apiReference.webhookNoRetryValue: Any 4xx other than 408 and 429 is never retried: it would fail identically.
apiReference.webhookDedupe: Deduplicate on X-GameDashboard-Delivery: that id is stable across attempts. Two endpoints subscribed to the same event do get two distinct deliveries, with two distinct ids.

password.tooShort: The password must be at least {minimum} characters long.
password.containsIdentity: The password must not contain your name or email address.
password.pwned: This password appears in {occurrences, plural, one {a known breach} other {# known breaches}}. Choose another one.
password.checkUnavailable: The breach check is unavailable. The password was accepted without it.

brandImage.formats: PNG, JPEG, WebP or ICO, 512 KiB at most (no SVG). Applied as soon as it is uploaded.

branding.title: White label
branding.subtitle: Your name, your logo and your colour, served on your own domain.
branding.imagesKeptBody: Changed after this page was opened, for instance by an image upload: the current value was kept ({fields}). The form now shows it; save again to replace it.
branding.inactiveTitle: Nothing is shown to your clients yet
branding.inactiveBody: The arrival domain picks the brand: until yours is verified, your clients see the platform's one, even though they are your clients.
branding.domainHint: A subdomain you own, pointed at the platform. The panel adds none to its web server configuration: it recognises yours from the request.
branding.domainLabelHint: No « https:// » and no path. Changing this name resets the verification.
branding.cnameHint: Routes traffic to the platform. Without it, your domain leads nowhere.
branding.txtHint: Proves the domain is yours. Under a dedicated label, since a CNAME excludes any other record at the same name.
branding.tlsTitle: Certificates are issued by the agent
branding.tlsBody: The panel recognises these domains but issues nothing itself: an agent runs on the web server, calls certbot and reports back here. A verified domain without a certificate serves a security warning to that reseller's customers.
branding.appearanceHint: Every field left empty falls back to the platform's: you only fill in what you change.
branding.name: Displayed name
branding.nameHint: Replaces « GameDashboard » in the header and the tab title.
branding.faviconHint: Optional: without it, your logo is used in the tab.
branding.accentHint: In hexadecimal notation, such as #0ea5e9. The light and dark tones are derived from it.
branding.loginTaglineHint: Shown under the logo on the sign-in screen.
branding.replyToHint: Emails sent to your customers carry your name; their replies go to this address. Empty: the platform's.
branding.urlHint: Full « https:// » address, or an internal path starting with « / ».

resellerDomains.title: Reseller domains
resellerDomains.subtitle: The names through which your resellers serve their own brand on this panel.
resellerDomains.tlsTitle: Every verified domain needs a certificate
resellerDomains.tlsBody: The panel recognises these domains without any change to its web configuration, but it does not issue their TLS certificate. Until a verified name has one, the reseller's clients hit a security warning.
resellerDomains.agentSilentTitle: The certificate agent has never reported
resellerDomains.agentSilentBody: Domains are verified, but no attempt has been recorded. The agent is probably not installed on the web server — until it runs, no certificate will be issued and the wait below will never end.
resellerDomains.certificateNotSought: None until the domain is verified
resellerDomains.emptyBody: A reseller declares their domain from their own area, then publishes a CNAME and a TXT record to prove ownership.

reseller.title: My fleet
reseller.subtitle: Your machines and shares, the servers you provisioned and the accounts they belong to.
reseller.provisioningOnNotice: The platform administration may create servers on your account. You can withdraw this from your settings.
reseller.provisioningOffNotice: Only you create servers on your machines. The platform administration cannot.
reseller.capacityHint: What you consume against what you are granted, machine by machine. On a shared dedicated box, your share only.
reseller.tenancyDedicatedHint: This machine is entrusted to you whole: its capacity is yours.
reseller.tenancySharedHint: You share this machine with other resellers. The figures shown are those of your share, not of the hardware.

usageBasis.estimated: Consumption not measured, capped by your limits
usageBasis.partial: Consumption partly measured, the rest capped by the limits

reseller.usageEstimatedNotice: {count} machine(s) without a recent measurement: their consumption is capped by the granted limits, so it reads higher than reality.
reseller.allocatedHint: Your consumption against the total granted to you: the figure that says whether it is time to ask for one more machine.
reseller.noNodesHint: No machine or share is assigned to you. Contact the platform administration.
reseller.nodesHint: The machines hosting your servers, driven by the Wings daemon. Their installation, token and maintenance remain the platform's responsibility.
reseller.portsSharedHint: This machine's ports are common to the resellers on it: the free count can drop without any action of yours.
reseller.serversHint: {shown} server(s) of {total}, belonging to your clients.
reseller.resizeHint: “{name}” keeps its files and its address. Memory and CPU apply right away; if the daemon cannot do it live, at the next start.
reseller.resizeMemoryHint: In megabytes. Any increase counts against your envelope and against the room left on the machine.
reseller.resizeCpuHint: As a percentage of one core: 100 is a whole core, 200 is two. Zero means no limit.
reseller.resizeSwapHint: In megabytes. Zero disables it; -1 makes it unlimited.
reseller.resizeBackupsHint: How many backups the client may keep. Zero forbids them.
reseller.resizeDatabasesHint: How many databases they may create.
reseller.resizePortsHint: How many ports they may reserve on the machine. At least one, or their server has no address.
reseller.resizeDiskHint: In megabytes. Shrinking erases nothing: files already written stay, but nothing more can be added beyond the new limit.
reseller.deleteServerBody: “{name}” and its volume will be erased. This cannot be undone: take a backup if anything on it matters.
reseller.noServersHint: You have not provisioned any server yet.
reseller.clientsHint: The accounts whose servers you host.
reseller.clientsTableHint: You see what consumes your resources, nothing of their account life.
reseller.noClientsHint: You do not host anyone's server yet.
reseller.settingsHint: What you let the platform do on your fleet.
reseller.provisioningHint: What is entrusted to you is your responsibility, and you answer for what runs on it.
reseller.provisioningLabel: Allow the administration to create servers on my account
reseller.provisioningLabelHint: Closed by default. Every change is written to the audit log.
reseller.provisioningOnBody: A platform administrator may now create servers that will belong to you, on your machines. You remain responsible for what runs there.
reseller.provisioningOffBody: Any attempt by the administration to create a server on your account is refused, with the reason shown.
reseller.quotaHint: What you may resell, across every machine — including your own nodes.
reseller.quotaUnlimitedHint: No allowance is set for you: only your machines' capacity bounds you.
reseller.quotaFullNotice: Your allowance is full: nothing can be created until the administration raises it.
reseller.quotaOverEnforcedNotice: Your memory usage exceeds your allowance. If it stays there, the heaviest server will be stopped to bring you back under the cap. Reduce usage, or ask the administration to raise the allowance.
reseller.quotaOverUnmeasuredNotice: Your usage appears to exceed your allowance, but it is estimated for lack of recent measurements: the figure is capped by the granted limits. No server will be stopped on that basis. Only creation stays blocked.
reseller.quotaOverPassiveNotice: Your allowance is exceeded on disk or server count. No server will be stopped — stopping one does not free any disk. Only creation is blocked.

schedules.title: Scheduled tasks
schedules.subtitle: Automate restarts, backups and recurring commands.
schedules.emptyHint: Schedule a nightly restart or a daily backup.
schedules.utcNotice: Times are in UTC, as on the node.
schedules.onlyWhenOnlineHint: The task is skipped while the server is offline, and its last-run date is left untouched.

security.title: Security
security.subtitle: Password, two-factor authentication and active sessions.
security.newPasswordHint: At least 12 characters. Checked against known breaches.
security.twoFactorHint: A second proof of identity at every sign-in.
security.sessionsHint: Devices currently signed in to your account.
security.revokeAllHint: Every other device must sign in again. This session stays active.
security.revokedCount: {count, plural, one {# session closed.} other {# sessions closed.}}
security.twoFactorOffHint: Today your password alone opens your account. A one-time code adds a proof only your phone can give.
security.enableConfirmBody: Your password first: a second factor on your account must only ever be set by you.
security.provisionalBody: This password was generated for a first sign-in. Choose your own: after twenty-four hours, it will be refused.
security.setupStep1: 1. Scan this code with your app
security.setupStep1Hint: Google Authenticator, Aegis, 1Password, Bitwarden — they all read the same format.
security.setupManual: Or type this key by hand
security.setupStep2Hint: Six digits. They change every thirty seconds.
security.recoveryHint: Write them down now: they will never be shown again. Each one opens your account once, if you lose your phone.
security.recoveryRemaining: {count, plural, =0 {No recovery code left} one {# recovery code left} other {# recovery codes left}}
security.recoveryRegenerateHint: The old ones stop working, including those never used.
security.recoveryNone: No recovery code. If you lose your phone, you lose access.
security.confirmPasswordHint: To check that it is really you in front of this screen.
security.disableBody: Your password alone will open your account again, and your recovery codes will be erased.
security.passkeysHint: A physical key, your fingerprint or your device unlock, instead of a code to copy.
security.passkeyAddHint: Your browser will ask which key to use: USB key, phone, or this device's unlock.
security.passkeyLabelHint: To recognise it in the list. Asked now, because after the ceremony you no longer know which one you just touched.
security.sshSectionHint: Your SSH public keys, to reach your servers' files over SFTP without handing over your password.
security.sshKeysHint: A key opens no new access: it applies to the servers your account already has rights on.
security.sshKeyAddHint: Paste the contents of your « .pub » file, on a single line.
security.sshKeyNameHint: Optional: the key's own comment is used when left empty.
security.sshKeyPrivateWarning: Never paste your private key — the one without « .pub ». The panel does not need it, and nobody should ask you for it.
security.passkeyRemoveBody: “{label}” will no longer open your account. The object itself is unchanged.
security.passkeyFailed: The key could not be used. Try again, or pick another method.
security.passwordChangedAnd: Password changed. {count, plural, one {# other session was closed.} other {# other sessions were closed.}}
security.pwnedCheckFailed: The known-breach check could not run: the third-party service did not answer. The password was changed.
security.mismatch: The two entries do not match.
security.problemTooShort: The password must be at least {minimum} characters long.
security.problemContainsIdentity: The password must not contain your name or your email address.
security.problemPwned: This password appears {occurrences, plural, one {# time} other {# times}} in known data breaches. Pick another one.

serverList.title: My servers
serverList.subtitle: The game servers you have access to.
serverList.emptyHint: You do not have access to any server yet.

serverSettings.title: Settings
serverSettings.subtitle: Identity, startup variables, SFTP access and advanced actions.
serverSettings.identityHint: Name shown in the panel. No effect on the game server.
serverSettings.variablesHint: Read by the Docker image at launch. Applied at the next start.
serverSettings.noVariables: This egg declares no client-visible variable.
serverSettings.sftpHint: Use these details in FileZilla or WinSCP.
serverSettings.sftpClosedBody: SFTP authentication is not being served by the panel right now. The details below are the node's, but the connection will be refused. Use the file manager meanwhile.
serverSettings.sftpKeyHint: You can also connect with an SSH key, without handing your password to your SFTP client:
serverSettings.resourcesHint: Set by your plan. Contact support to change them.
serverSettings.dangerZoneHint: These actions affect the server's data.
serverSettings.reinstallHint: Re-runs the install script over the existing files. Configuration files may be overwritten, and this cannot be undone.
serverSettings.reinstallBody: The install script runs again over the existing volume. Take a backup first.
serverSettings.dockerImageHint: Chosen among those the egg declares. The server must be restarted for it to take effect.

staffTwoFactor.title: Second proof required
staffTwoFactor.body: This platform requires its staff and resellers to provide a second proof of identity. Until it is enabled on your account, this area stays closed — the API refuses it too.
staffTwoFactor.emptyBody: Enable an authenticator app or a passkey, then come back here.

status.title: Platform status
status.subtitle: Component health and ongoing incidents. Public page, readable without an account.

stateBody.operational: No component reports a problem and no incident is open.
stateBody.maintenance: A planned intervention is under way. Affected services may be unavailable for its duration.
stateBody.degraded: Part of the platform is not working normally. Details below.
stateBody.down: One or more components are down. Details below.

status.apiUnreachableBody: This page could not reach the panel API. That is itself a sign of an outage: if it persists, treat the platform as unavailable.
status.componentsHint: The platform's machines. Reseller fleets are not listed here.
status.uptimeTooEarly: Uptime tracked for less than an hour

subusers.title: Sub-users
subusers.subtitle: Grant limited access to your server, one permission at a time.
subusers.emptyHint: Invite a teammate to share managing the server.
subusers.pendingInvitesHint: These addresses do not have an account yet. The link stays valid until its expiry date, or until you cancel it.
subusers.inviteBody: They must already have a GameDashboard account. The server appears in their list and they must accept the access.
subusers.presetHint: Ticks a set of permissions. Adjust them after: the boxes are what counts, not the preset.
subusers.editBody: {name} — open consoles will be closed so the change takes effect.
subusers.removeBody: {name} loses access to this server, and their console closes immediately.

webhooks.title: Outbound callbacks
webhooks.hint: What the panel tells the third-party system: install finished, suspension, deletion. The application API goes one way, callbacks the other.
webhooks.createHint: The signing secret is shown once.
webhooks.noKeysBody: A callback hangs off a key: issue one first, just above.
webhooks.keyHint: Revoking the key takes its callbacks with it: a cut-off system never keeps being called.
webhooks.urlHint: Over https. The signature proves origin, it does not encrypt the content.
webhooks.secretOnceBody: It verifies the signature of every callback. It will never be shown again; if lost, rotate it.
webhooks.emptyHint: Nothing is sent anywhere. The third party has to poll the API to learn what happened.
webhooks.deleteBody: Pending deliveries go with it. The third-party system stops being notified.
webhooks.noDeliveriesHint: Nothing sent yet: no subscribed event has occurred.

engine.title: Server engine
engine.subtitle: What this server runs: its platform, or the modpack that replaces it along with everything around it.
engine.platformsHint: The program itself. The file is placed under the name the egg expects, and the server is stopped before anything is touched.
engine.packsHint: A platform, its mods and their settings in one piece, from Modrinth or CurseForge. The archive is opened inside the container, then each mod is downloaded by the daemon; the server pack is preferred when the author publishes one. The loader the pack asks for is installed too: Fabric directly, Forge and NeoForge through their official installer, run by a reinstallation of the Minecraft Java egg.
engine.noPlatformHint: The publishers did not answer, or none suits this server's loader. Try again later.
engine.beforeYouStartBody: The server is stopped automatically, then what is there is overwritten. Take a backup if its contents matter: nothing replaced can be recovered from this screen.
engine.confirmJarBody: The server program is replaced. Worlds, plugins and configurations stay in place — only the startup file changes.
engine.confirmPackBody: The modpack pours its mods and configuration files over the existing tree. Anything with the same name is overwritten, and that cannot be undone.
engine.eulaBody: A Minecraft server refuses to start until Mojang's licence agreement is accepted. The panel does not accept it for you.
engine.eulaDialogIntro: Mojang requires the operator of a server to accept its licence agreement before running it. This acceptance binds you, not the host.
engine.eulaWhoBody: Your account and the date of your acceptance are written to the server's activity log, and into the container's eula.txt file.
engine.eulaConfirm: I have read Minecraft's licence agreement and I accept it for this server.
engine.confirmEulaReset: Acceptance of the Minecraft licence agreement will be withdrawn: this server will no longer run the same program, and it will have to be accepted again before starting it.
engine.confirmUpdateBody: Files placed by the previous version of the pack are replaced, and those it no longer contains are removed. The server is stopped during the operation.
engine.preservedBody: Never overwritten: worlds, server.properties and player lists. A pack configuration file modified since it was installed (size or date changed) is kept as is. What the panel cannot detect: a file you created under a name the pack also uses is overwritten, and a configuration rewritten by a mod at startup counts as modified, so it is not updated.
engine.loaderBody: A Forge or NeoForge pack has its loader installed by a reinstallation of the egg: the publisher's installer downloads its libraries, which adds a few minutes. Worlds, mods and configurations stay in place.
engine.backupFirstHint: A regular server backup, taken with the server stopped; the installation waits for it to finish, and stops without writing anything if it fails.
engine.backupUnavailable: No prior backup is possible here (zero quota or missing permission): what is replaced cannot be recovered from this screen.
engine.currentTracked: {count, plural, one {# pack file tracked} other {# pack files tracked}}
engine.upToDate: Up to date for this Minecraft version.
engine.notCheckedYet: Updates for this pack will be checked within the hour.
engine.reportWritten: {files} file(s) placed, {removed} file(s) from the previous version removed.
engine.reportKept: Kept as is (modified since, or belonging to the server): {files}.
engine.installRunningBody: The server is stopped while the installation runs, including the backup taken first. This page updates by itself; you can leave it, the installation carries on.

adminServerDetail.subtitle: {egg} on {node} — settings the client area does not offer.
adminServerDetail.transferHint: The server is stopped, its files are copied to the chosen machine, then its address changes. How long it takes depends on the size of its disk.
adminServerDetail.noDestination: No other node is declared: there is nowhere to move this server to.
adminServerDetail.transferBusyBody: This server is in state « {state} ». The move will wait until it is available.
adminServerDetail.transferConfirmBody: The server will be stopped, copied to « {node} », then started there. Its address will change: remember to pass it on to its players.
adminServerDetail.changeEggHint: Move this server to another game without deleting it: it keeps its identifier, its subusers, its schedules and its history.
adminServerDetail.noOtherEgg: No other game is enabled on this platform.
adminServerDetail.newEggHint: Only games an administrator has enabled are offered.
adminServerDetail.eggReinstallHint: Runs the new game's installation script inside the container. This is what installs Forge, NeoForge and every game that is not just a file to drop in.
adminServerDetail.eggWipeBody: The new game's installation script runs over the existing volume: it may overwrite configuration files and worlds. The old game's variables, startup command and image are replaced by the new one's. Take a backup first if the files matter.
adminServerDetail.eggKeepTitle: The server will not start yet
adminServerDetail.eggKeepBody: Without a reinstall, the server will carry the new game's name while its files are still the old one's. That is useful to fix a record, but someone will have to run the reinstall before the next start.
adminServerDetail.changeEggConfirmWipe: This server moves to « {egg} » and its installation script runs over the existing files. This cannot be undone.
adminServerDetail.changeEggConfirmKeep: This server moves to « {egg} » without touching its files. A reinstall will be needed before starting it again.
adminServerDetail.changeOwnerHint: The server moves to another account. Its host does not change: the reseller link says who hosts, not who owns.
adminServerDetail.changeOwnerFieldHint: Subusers invited to this server keep their access.
adminServerDetail.runtimeHint: Container image and startup command. The daemon re-reads the configuration on save; the change takes effect on the next start.
adminServerDetail.unresolvedBody: {names} has no value. Wings replaces an empty placeholder with nothing — it does not leave it as is — so the command will go out truncated and the server will not start.
adminServerDetail.dockerImageHint: The offered images are those the egg declares. The field stays free for an image you maintain yourself.
adminServerDetail.startupHint: Placeholders written between double braces are replaced by the variables below at start time.
adminServerDetail.variablesHint: Including those closed to the owner: “not editable” bounds what a client may change, not what you may repair.
adminServerDetail.oomKillerHint: Enabled, the container is stopped outright as soon as it exceeds its memory limit — the ongoing game is lost, but the machine is protected. Disabled, it slows down without ever stopping, and can drag its neighbours with it.
adminServerDetail.editLimitsHint: The server keeps its files and its address. Memory and CPU apply right away; if the daemon cannot do it live, at the next start. Any increase counts against the hosting reseller's envelope and against the room left on the machine.
adminServerDetail.diskHint: In megabytes. Shrinking erases nothing: files already written stay, but nothing more can be added beyond the new limit.
adminServerDetail.swapHint: In megabytes. Zero disables swap; -1 makes it unlimited.
adminServerDetail.cpuHint: As a percentage of one core: 100 is a whole core, 200 is two. Zero means no limit.
adminServerDetail.backupLimitHint: How many backups the client may keep.
adminServerDetail.databaseLimitHint: How many databases they may create.
adminServerDetail.allocationLimitHint: How many ports they may reserve on the machine.

retention.title: Database housekeeping
retention.subtitle: What the platform deletes automatically, and what it keeps.
retention.failureTitle: {count, plural, =1 {The last sweep failed} other {# sweeps in a row failed}}
retention.removedRows: {count, plural, =1 {1 row removed} other {# rows removed}}

adminUpdates.title: Updates
adminUpdates.subtitle: The panel updates itself from GitHub releases: each new version is tried on its own before switching over.
adminUpdates.stepRepetition: Trying {version} on its own before switching
adminUpdates.resultErrorHint: Nothing changed for visitors; the next check will try again.
adminUpdates.refused: Versions set aside: {versions}. They will not be tried again; the next release will be.
adminUpdates.checkStarted: Check started: the status will update here.
adminUpdates.rollbackTitle: Go back to the previous version?
adminUpdates.rollbackBody: The panel will switch back to {previous} and set {current} aside: it will not be reinstalled. Database migrations are not undone.
adminUpdates.rollbackDone: Rollback requested: the panel is restarting on {version}.

serverWebhooks.title: Outgoing webhooks
serverWebhooks.subtitle: Have an endpoint notified when something happens to this server.
serverWebhooks.declareHint: The panel will send a signed request to this address. The signing secret is shown only once.
serverWebhooks.urlHint: A public “https://” address. Loopback and private networks are refused.
serverWebhooks.emptyHint: Add an endpoint to be notified without opening the panel.
serverWebhooks.secretHint: Copy it now: it will never be shown again. It proves that requests really come from the panel.
serverWebhooks.deleteBody: Nothing more will be sent to {url}. Its history goes with it.

errorPage.subtitle: GameDashboard panel
errorPage.recovering: The API is answering again. Reloading…
errorPage.exhaustedTitle: The API answers, but the page still fails
errorPage.exhaustedBody: The panel retried {count} times without success. The cause is therefore not — or no longer — the API: check its logs, then try again.
errorPage.databaseBody: The API is running but cannot reach PostgreSQL. Restarting it would change nothing: it is the database that needs to be brought back.
errorPage.timeoutTitle: The API is taking too long to answer
errorPage.timeoutBody: The connection was accepted, but no answer arrived in time. This is not a stopped process: look instead for a saturated database, a blocked query or a node that does not hand back control.
errorPage.downBody: The panel reads its data from the API, which is not running. Start it in a second terminal: the page will resume by itself as soon as it answers.
errorPage.noteRecovering: The API is answering again. Reloading…

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.description: This page does not exist or you do not have access to it.

passwordStrength.missing: {count, plural, one {# more character} other {# more characters}}
passwordStrength.identityHint: it contains your name or email address
passwordStrength.longerHint: a longer one would be safer
passwordStrength.breachHint: it will also be checked against known breaches

securityAlerts.failureSubject: Failed sign-in attempts on your {brand} account
securityAlerts.failureBody: {count} sign-in attempts on your account failed in a row. The last one came from {ip}, on {time}.
securityAlerts.failureAdvice: If this was not you, someone may be trying to guess your password. Change it and turn on two-factor authentication:
securityAlerts.failureReassure: If this was you, there is nothing to do. After ten failures, sign-ins to this account are paused for a few minutes.
securityAlerts.newDeviceBody: Your account was just opened from a device or network it had never used before.
securityAlerts.newDeviceAdvice: If this was not you, sign out your other sessions and change your password:
securityAlerts.newDeviceReassure: If this was you, you can ignore this message.
securityAlerts.footer: This security message is sent regardless of your notification settings.

credentialBody.passwordChanged: The password of your account was just changed, and your other sessions were signed out.
credentialBody.passwordReset: The password of your account was just reset through a link sent to this address, and every session was signed out.
credentialBody.twoFactorEnabled: Two-factor authentication with an app was just turned on for your account.
credentialBody.twoFactorDisabled: Two-factor authentication with an app was just turned off for your account.
credentialBody.passkeyAdded: A new passkey was just registered on your account.
credentialBody.passkeyRemoved: A passkey was just removed from your account.
credentialBody.emailChanged: The email address of your account was just replaced. This message goes to the former address; the next ones will go to the new one.

securityAlerts.credentialAdvice: If this was not you, someone may have taken over your account: change your password, sign out your other sessions and check your two-factor authentication:
securityAlerts.credentialReassure: If this was you, there is nothing to do.
securityAlerts.emailChangedAdvice: If you did not ask for this, contact your host's support right away: this account now signs in with the new address.

subuserPresets.title: Subuser presets
subuserPresets.description: The permissions each preset ticks in the invitation form, on every server of the platform.
subuserPresets.existingBody: A subuser's permissions are copied when they are invited. Changing a preset only affects future invitations: nobody gains or loses a right retroactively.
subuserPresets.savedBody: Future invitations will start from these presets.
subuserPresets.resetBody: The three presets go back to the values shipped with the panel. Existing subusers keep their permissions.

adminEggEditor.subtitle: Family “{nest}”. An egg describes how to install and run a game: Docker image, startup command, settings offered to the customer.
adminEggEditor.savedBody: Egg saved. Syncing its source repository will no longer overwrite it.
adminEggEditor.inUseTitle: {count, plural, one {# server uses this egg} other {# servers use this egg}}
adminEggEditor.inUseBody: Your changes apply to these servers on their next start or reinstall. A variable they use cannot be removed or renamed, and stricter rules are refused if they reject a current value.
adminEggEditor.detachNotice: This egg comes from a synced repository. Once edited here, syncing will no longer overwrite it: your changes are kept, and repository updates stop applying to it.
adminEggEditor.confirmTitle: {count, plural, one {Edit an egg used by # server?} other {Edit an egg used by # servers?}}
adminEggEditor.confirmBody: Existing servers keep their current image and startup command; everything else (install script, configuration, variables) applies on their next start or reinstall. Added variables get their default value on each of them.
adminEggEditor.fixFields: {count, plural, one {One field needs fixing: it is highlighted in red.} other {# fields need fixing: they are highlighted in red.}}
adminEggEditor.exportHint: Downloads the egg in Pterodactyl format (PTDL_v2), importable here or into Pterodactyl.
adminEggEditor.identityHint: What the customer reads when picking a game.
adminEggEditor.name: Name
adminEggEditor.nameHint: The game or variant name, as shown in the catalogue.
adminEggEditor.author: Author
adminEggEditor.authorHint: Contact address of the egg author. Optional.
adminEggEditor.descriptionHint: One or two sentences: what this server does, what sets it apart from other variants.
adminEggEditor.startupHint: The command run in the container, and the one that stops it cleanly.
adminEggEditor.startupFieldHint: Variables are written between double braces. SERVER_MEMORY, SERVER_PORT and SERVER_IP are provided by the panel.
adminEggEditor.startupPreviewHint: This is the command a new server will run. Anything still between braces is computed per server (memory, port) or matches no variable: check the spelling.
adminEggEditor.stopHint: Sent to the console to stop the game cleanly. ^C sends an interrupt signal.
adminEggEditor.imagesHint: The environments the game can run in. The first one is used for new servers; the customer can pick any of the others.
adminEggEditor.variablesHint: The egg settings. Each becomes an environment variable of the container and can be referenced in the startup command.
adminEggEditor.variablesEmptyHint: Add one to let the customer choose, for example, the game version.
adminEggEditor.variableServers: {count, plural, =0 {No servers} one {# server} other {# servers}}
adminEggEditor.variableInUse: Servers have a value for this variable: it cannot be removed or renamed. To hide it from the customer, untick “Visible to the customer”.
adminEggEditor.variableNameHint: What the customer reads above the field.
adminEggEditor.variableEnvHint: Upper case, letters, digits and “_”. This is the name used in the startup command.
adminEggEditor.variableEnvLocked: Used by servers: the name can no longer change.
adminEggEditor.variableDescriptionHint: One sentence shown under the field, saying what it is for.
adminEggEditor.variableDefaultHint: Given to every new server. It must satisfy the rules.
adminEggEditor.variableRulesHint: Separated by “|”. required: mandatory; nullable: may stay empty; max, min, between: length or value; in: closed list; regex: pattern.
adminEggEditor.variableViewableHint: The customer sees the variable and its value in their server startup settings.
adminEggEditor.variableEditableHint: The customer can change the value, which is then checked against the rules above. Requires the variable to be visible.
adminEggEditor.installHint: The script run once, when a server is created or reinstalled, in a separate container. It downloads the game into /mnt/server.
adminEggEditor.installContainerHint: The image the script runs in. It must contain the tools the script uses (curl, jq…).
adminEggEditor.installEntrypointHint: bash, ash or sh depending on the image.
adminEggEditor.installScriptHint: Review it before enabling the egg: it runs with the container's rights on every installed server.
adminEggEditor.advancedHint: Read by the daemon as is: startup detection, files rewritten on every start, logs. Rarely needs changing.
adminEggEditor.advancedCollapsed: Collapsed. Most imported eggs already carry a correct configuration.
adminEggEditor.configStartupHint: JSON object. “done” is the console text that signals the game is ready: the server then goes “online”.
adminEggEditor.configFilesHint: JSON object. For each file, the values the daemon rewrites before every start (port, address).
adminEggEditor.featuresHint: One per line. They enable game-specific helpers (EULA acceptance, Java version choice).
adminEggEditor.fileDenylistHint: One pattern per line. The customer can neither read nor edit these files from the file manager.

problems.envFormat: Letters, digits and “_” only, not starting with a digit. Example: GAME_VERSION.
problems.envReserved: Reserved name: the panel sets this variable itself. Pick another one.
problems.duplicate: Already used above: each name must be unique.
problems.imagesEmpty: Add at least one Docker image: without one, the server cannot start.
problems.jsonObject: JSON object expected (between braces). Check the quotes and commas.
problems.unknownVariable: This variable no longer exists on the egg. Reload the page.
problems.defaultBreaksRules: The default value does not satisfy the variable rules: fix one or the other.
problems.editableHidden: An editable variable must be visible to the customer.
problems.rulesEmpty: Enter at least one rule, for example required|string.
problems.ruleUnknown: Rule “{rule}” is unknown to the panel: it would not be applied. See the examples.
problems.ruleNeedsNumber: Rule “{rule}” expects a number, for example max:20.
problems.ruleNeedsTwoNumbers: Rule “between” expects two numbers, for example between:1,10.
problems.ruleInEmpty: Rule “in” expects a list of values, for example in:yes,no.
problems.ruleRegexInvalid: Unreadable regular expression. Write it between slashes, for example regex:/^[a-z]+$/.

adminEggEditor.consoleCommandsHint: One per line, arguments in angle brackets. Suggested while typing in the console; nothing runs unless typed.

nodeAdmin.title: Machines (nodes)
nodeAdmin.intro: A node is a physical or virtual machine that hosts game servers. The panel drives it remotely through the Wings daemon installed on it. Click a machine to open its sheet.
nodeAdmin.emptyBody: Start by adding a machine: the panel guides you through declaring it, installing Wings on it and checking that it answers. You will then give it ports.
nodeAdmin.emptyNeedsLocation: First create a location ("Classification" button): a machine cannot be declared without one. Then come back to add the machine.
nodeAdmin.capacityLegend: The gauges show what is promised to servers (their limits), not what they consume: that is what tells whether there is room for one more server.
nodeAdmin.outdatedHint: A newer Wings version ({latest}) runs elsewhere in the fleet.
nodeAdmin.measuredNow: {used} in use right now · {count, plural, one {# server measured} other {# servers measured}}
nodeAdmin.measuredNone: No recent usage measured: the machine is unreachable, or none of its servers has run.
nodeAdmin.reasonNeverSeen: The Wings daemon has never contacted the panel yet: it is not installed, not started, or cannot reach the panel. See the "Installation and token" section.

reason.online: All good: the daemon answers and its servers can be driven normally.
reason.stale: The daemon has not reported for over a minute. Often a slow network; after two minutes the machine will be declared unreachable.
reason.maintenance: The machine no longer accepts new servers; those running on it carry on normally.
reason.unreachable: The panel no longer hears from the daemon: servers on this machine can no longer be started, stopped or inspected from here. Check that Wings is running on the machine.

nodeAdmin.overallocationNote: Overallocation: {memory}% memory, {disk}% disk. The gauges account for this allowed excess.
nodeAdmin.locationHint: Where the machine lives. Customers sometimes pick their server by location.
nodeAdmin.fqdnHint: The address through which the panel and browsers reach the daemon, e.g. node1.example.com.
nodeAdmin.fqdnCreateHint: The machine's full address, e.g. node1.example.com. With https, an IP address will not do: it cannot carry a valid certificate.
nodeAdmin.protocolHint: https is recommended: mandatory as soon as the panel itself is served over https.
nodeAdmin.protocolHttpWarning: Over http, this machine's console will not work from a panel served over https: the browser refuses a clear-text connection from an encrypted page. Keep this for a development box.
nodeAdmin.daemonPortHint: Port on which Wings listens for the panel's orders. 8080 by default.
nodeAdmin.sftpPortHint: Port through which customers transfer their files. 2022 by default.
nodeAdmin.settingsPanelHint: These settings only concern the panel: nothing is sent to the machine, and saving is immediate.
nodeAdmin.nameHint: A short name to recognise it in lists, e.g. RYZEN-09.
nodeAdmin.categoryHint: Optional: used to sort machines in the list (range, provider…).
nodeAdmin.memoryCreateHint: The memory you are willing to sell, in MB. 64 GB = 65536.
nodeAdmin.diskCreateHint: Disk space for servers, in MB. 500 GB = 512000.
nodeAdmin.cpuHint: Number of cores on the machine. Decimals accepted.
nodeAdmin.capacityFloor: Already promised to servers: {promised}. Capacity cannot go below it.
nodeAdmin.overallocateHint: Percentage sold beyond the hardware, since servers do not use their full limit. 0 = no excess. Resulting capacity: {total}.
nodeAdmin.capacityTooLow: {resource}: {capacity} requested, but {promised} are already promised to servers. Keep at least what is promised, raise the overallocation, or move servers first.
nodeAdmin.publicHint: When unchecked, the machine only hosts servers the administration places there itself.
nodeAdmin.ownerCreateHint: Can be changed later from the sheet, "Resellers" section.
nodeAdmin.bindingTitle: Address and ports — the machine's config.yml
nodeAdmin.bindingHint: These values also live in the Wings configuration file on the machine. Changing them on one side only would cut the panel off from the machine: the panel therefore changes them together with the daemon.
nodeAdmin.bindingHowPush: The panel sends the new configuration to the daemon, at its current address.
nodeAdmin.bindingHowCheck: It then checks that the daemon answers at the new address. Nothing is saved in the panel before that proof.
nodeAdmin.bindingHowRestart: A port change only takes effect when Wings restarts: the screen will say so, and you will just need to confirm again after the restart.

bindingProblem.fqdn_needs_domain: With https, enter a domain name: an IP address cannot carry a valid certificate.
bindingProblem.ports_collide: The daemon port and the SFTP port must differ: only one program can listen on a port.

nodeAdmin.bindingApplied: The daemon answers at the new address: the change is saved.
nodeAdmin.bindingUnchanged: Nothing changed: these are already the saved values.
nodeAdmin.bindingRestartBody: The daemon saved the new configuration but still listens at the old address. Nothing changed in the panel meanwhile. On the machine, run the command below, then click "Confirm again".
nodeAdmin.bindingRefusedTitle: The daemon could not be updated — nothing changed
nodeAdmin.bindingRefusedBody: Put the file below in place of /etc/pterodactyl/config.yml yourself, restart Wings, then confirm again. The file holds the machine's token: treat it like a password.
nodeAdmin.portsAddHint: Each game server listens on a port of the machine. Without a free port, no server can be created on it.
nodeAdmin.portsIpHint: The machine's public IP address, the one players will use.
nodeAdmin.portRangeHint: A range, e.g. 25565 to 25575. Ports 1024 to 65535.
nodeAdmin.portsAdded: Ports added. Those that already existed were skipped.
nodeAdmin.portsStockHint: A port used by a server cannot be removed: free it from the server, or delete the server.
nodeAdmin.portsRemoveTitle: Remove {count, plural, one {# port} other {# ports}}?
nodeAdmin.portsRemoveBody: They leave the stock of "{name}": no new server will be able to use them. No existing server is affected.
nodeAdmin.portsRemoved: {count, plural, one {# port removed} other {# ports removed}}.
nodeAdmin.portsEmptyHint: Add a range above: it is required to create a server on this machine.
nodeAdmin.installHint: To do on the machine, once and for all, or to set a daemon straight again.
nodeAdmin.tokenHint: The secret that binds the machine to the panel, both ways. Replacing it is safe: the panel only keeps the new one once the daemon has confirmed it knows it.
nodeAdmin.tokenRotated: Token replaced and confirmed by the daemon.
nodeAdmin.sharesSectionBody: Several resellers can share the machine, each with its own share of memory, disk and servers.
nodeAdmin.maintenanceHint: Turn on before working on the machine.
nodeAdmin.maintenanceEffect: No new server will be placed on it. {count, plural, =0 {No server runs on it.} one {The server running on it carries on normally.} other {The # servers running on it carry on normally.}}
nodeAdmin.removeBlocked: Not possible yet: {count, plural, one {# server is hosted on it} other {# servers are hosted on it}}. Transfer or delete them first.
nodeAdmin.removeWhat: The machine leaves the fleet with its declared ports. Its token is lost: an already installed Wings will no longer be able to talk to the panel.
nodeAdmin.removeTypeName: Type the machine's name to confirm.
nodeAdmin.wizardIntro: Four steps: declare it to the panel, install Wings on it, wait for it to report, then give it ports.

wizardStepHint.declare: What the panel needs to know about the machine. Nothing is installed yet.
wizardStepHint.install: On the machine, as root, with Wings already downloaded. The command fetches its configuration from the panel.
wizardStepHint.contact: The panel waits for the daemon to report. Keep this page open.

nodeAdmin.contactWaiting: Waiting for the first contact from "{name}"… ({seconds} s)
nodeAdmin.contactSlowTitle: Still nothing? Check on the machine:
nodeAdmin.contactSlowService: that Wings is running: systemctl status wings;
nodeAdmin.contactSlowFirewall: that the firewall lets the daemon port and the SFTP port through;
nodeAdmin.contactSlowPanel: that the machine can reach the panel's address (the one in the command);
nodeAdmin.doneBody: "{name}" has contacted the panel: Wings is installed and configured.
nodeAdmin.doneNextPorts: Last step: add ports. Without them, no server can be created on this machine.

adminUserEdit.editHint: Account {email}. The role is changed from the row menu; only the holder chooses the password.
adminUserEdit.emailChangeWarning: The new address will become "unverified" again: a confirmation email will be sent to it, and links already sent to the old one will stop working.
adminUserEdit.localeHint: Language of this account's screens and emails.
adminUserEdit.savedVerificationSent: Account updated. A confirmation email was sent to {email}.
adminUserEdit.savedVerificationNotSent: Account updated, but no confirmation email could be sent (mail not configured or too many requests). The address stays unverified.
adminUserEdit.resetBody: A link valid for one hour goes to {email}. The holder will choose their new password there: you will never see it. The old one stays valid until the link is used.
adminUserEdit.suspendHint: What happens as soon as you confirm:
adminUserEdit.suspendEffectLogin: no sign-in is possible any more: password, passkey, SSO, billing link;
adminUserEdit.suspendEffectSessions: their open sessions and consoles are closed immediately;
adminUserEdit.suspendEffectKeys: their API keys, their shop's keys if they are a reseller, and their SFTP access are refused;
adminUserEdit.suspendEffectServers: their servers keep running. To stop them, suspend them separately.
adminUserEdit.reasonHint: Internal: visible to administration and support, never to the holder.
adminUserEdit.suspended: Account suspended. {count, plural, =0 {No session was open.} one {# session closed.} other {# sessions closed.}}
adminUserEdit.reactivateBody: Suspension reason: {reason}. The holder will be able to sign in again; their API keys and SFTP will work again.

players.title: Players
players.subtitle: Who is online, and the game's moderation commands.
players.actHint: The panel types the command declared by the game into the console. The player may be offline.
players.noProbeHint: The panel checks the server every minute while it runs. Start it, or wait for the next check.
players.emptyHint: You can still ban or whitelist an offline player.
players.partial: The game only reports some of the connected players: the list below is a sample.
players.noCommands: No moderation commands for this game
players.noCommandsHint: This server's egg declares no player commands (player_commands key). Use the console instead.
players.reasonHint: Optional. Shown to the player by the game.
